_purpose: Conformance fixture for the header contract (see the 'Custom headers and variable resolution' section of docs/DEV_MCP.md). Three executors build requests from the same definition — the Dev MCP from disk, the Test MCP from api_library, and the ProjexLight backend for the UI's quick/chain/workflow/dataset/manual modes. Each must produce the SAME headers for the inputs below. Without this check the three drift within a release, and the drift is invisible until a staging run disagrees with a laptop.
_how_to_run: Dev MCP: dist/parity/check_parity.py. Test MCP and ProjexLight executor: feed the same config+definition and compare against expected[]. A mismatch is a contract violation in whichever executor differs, not a reason to edit this file.

cases.name: layer precedence: env beats default, provider matches, role applies
cases._note: x-api-key MUST resolve to the ENVIRONMENT value. If an executor returns 'GLOBAL-MUST-NOT-WIN' it is resolving global over environment, which would carry a dev secret into staging (MUST-46).

cases.name: provider and role headers do not leak to unrelated endpoints
cases._note: A layer that applies everywhere is worse than no layer — it silently re-identifies every request.

cases.name: dataset headers override configuration
cases._note: Layer 6 is last for a reason: a negative case must be able to send a deliberately wrong value.

cases.name: noAuth dataset sends no Authorization
cases._note: A dataset expecting 401 with no Authorization of its own is treated as noAuth. Injecting a valid token makes its assertion impossible to satisfy — this was 8 of 11 failures in a real ProjexCloud run.

cases.name: computed signature covers the exact body bytes
cases._note: Computed last, over the finalised body. An executor that signs before the body is complete produces a header the server rejects — a 401 that reads as a broken endpoint.
